transcript: Never ever ignore these four strange signals your body sends you, especially when anxiety is behind them. Stay with me until the last. That one quietly confuses the most people. First, anxiety can tighten your throat. It may feel like there is a lump that will not go away, not illness, but tension. The body holding itself as if danger is near. Second, your breathing begins to feel off. You try to take a full breath, but it never feels enough. Your chest tightens. Your heart may race. This is anxiety activating your fight-or-flight response, preparing you to act even when there is nothing to face. Third, tingling, numbness or sudden dizziness. When anxiety rises, blood flow shifts toward the muscles and so your hands, legs, even your head may feel strange or light. It feels serious, but often it is the body reacting, not failing. And fourth, the one that unsettles the mind the most, a feeling of being disconnected like you are not fully inside your body or the world around you feels unreal. This is anxiety at its peak. Your system overwhelmed, trying to protect you. Listen carefully. Anxiety can mimic many things, but it is not the end of you. It is a signal, not a sentence. If this message found you at the right moment, pause, breathe slowly and bring your body back to stillness. And if you want a simple path to calm your mind and reset your system, I wrote something for you. The monk's 30-day mind reset. It's in the link on my profile. You were not created to live in constant fear and you do not have to face it alone.
